answer: Require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can influence a market, then slash that stake if its claims fail independent challenge or its behavior violates agreed rules. Splitting one operator into a nebula of identities does not multiply voting power: every identity must lock scarce capital, and coordinated accounts risk losing it together when evidence links their actions. A gale of cheap sign-ups therefore cannot trigger a spiral of free influence; the attacker pays in locked funds, opportunity cost, and potential forfeiture.
